hero.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
hero.body:
Two prominent members of Ron DeSantis' communications team have publicly alleged that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, operated anonymous social media accounts to promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking the Governor. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both presented evidence linking the accounts to the Second Lady.

Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador indicating that the account @FSUdude01670 was connected to a phone number and email address matching ones known to be associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots of two-factor authentication messages sent to an email address with letters concealed and a phone number showing only the final digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she also said appeared tied to Layla Collins. According to Pushaw's posts, the account's content focused entirely on promoting Jay Collins and attacking individuals who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Pushaw noted that someone serving on an important state board, as Layla Collins does on the Board of Education, would typically lack time to maintain burner accounts so actively.

Redfern corroborated the findings, stating that the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated shortly after Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public, suggesting the individuals behind them were aware of the exposure. The sudden removal of the accounts came after the criticism appeared online.

The controversy creates a significant challenge for the final six months of DeSantis' gubernatorial term. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year and appointed Layla Collins to the state Board of Education. Jay Collins is competing in the Republican primary for Governor against U.S. Representative Byron Donalds, who has received the endorsement of Attorney General Uthmeier. As of late June, Collins had raised less than 3.5 million dollars, considerably trailing Donalds' fundraising efforts. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis before their current positions. Florida Politics has requested comment from both Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million for Governor's race as opponents struggle to keep pace
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds' campaign for Governor has raised $90 million, with nearly $10 million in his campaign account and more than $76.2 million in his political committee, while his Republican primary opponents lag far behind.
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has raised $90 million for his gubernatorial campaign, according to Division of Elections records through June 26. His campaign account received nearly $10 million in contributions, while his Friends of Byron Donalds political committee raised more than $76.2 million. Between June 20 and June 26 alone, Donalds raised nearly $2 million, with major contributors including GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. Donalds has invested heavily in his campaign with a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms. He has also consolidated endorsements from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison.

In stark contrast, Lt. Gov. Jay Collins raised only $15,500 in hard money and $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the same week, with less than $3.5 million total as of June 26. Collins struggled during a Friday night debate, fumbling answers on issues ranging from data centers to voting for DeSantis in 2018, which he could not do because he was not a Florida resident at that time. Collins lost his temper at various points during the debate and needed notes to help with responses.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man died in a head-on collision on State Road 710 in Martin County early Sunday morning, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash occurred around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

The FHP investigation determined that a 2015 Kia Optima traveling north on SR-710 drifted into the southbound lane and struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on. The left front of the Kia hit the left front of the Tundra. The impact caused the Kia to catch fire. The vehicle came to rest on the grass shoulder, still facing north. The Tundra ended up facing southeast in the southbound lane after the collision.

The Kia driver, a 40-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene. The Tundra driver, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was airlifted from the scene by Lifestar. The FHP continues to investigate the circumstances of the crash.

The identities of both drivers have not been released. Anyone with information about the crash is encouraged to contact the Florida Highway Patrol.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: President Trump's actions draw comparisons to monarchy as nation marks 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: The 250th anniversary of America's independence from Britain has sparked debate about presidential power, as President Donald Trump's second term actions lead historians to draw parallels with King George III.
cards.body:
The 250th anniversary of America's liberation from a king opened with a campaign-style rally on the National Mall by President Donald Trump, whose face adorns banners fluttering from federal buildings across the nation's capital. Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered the Department of Justice to pursue his political enemies, deployed the U.S. Marines to the nation's second largest city, and leveraged the presidency to enrich himself and his family. He has demanded that comedians who mock him be fired, slapped his name on the Kennedy Center, pushed to seize control of elections, filed lawsuits against news organizations whose coverage he disliked, and sued his own government seeking $10 billion in taxpayer money.

Trump's actions have drawn comparisons to King George III, the British monarch whose rule inspired the American Revolution. Trump rejected the comparison in a CBS "60 Minutes" interview, saying "I'm not a king. If I was a king, I wouldn't be dealing with you." Princeton University historian Julian Zelizer said the label reflects how Trump perceives himself and the presidency. When King Charles III visited Trump, the official White House X account posted an image of both men captioned "TWO KINGS." At the start of his second term, Trump posted "LONG LIVE THE KING" after announcing he had ended a New York City transportation program.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation attracts international artists to Fort Pierce with residency program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists through a residency program.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain at the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce. Mr. Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character, keeping it approximately 90 percent as it was when the Crains lived there. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, beginning with seven original birds that have grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and receives hand-feeding daily in his own bowls. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with art director Krystal Masters leading one-on-one classes for complete beginners in mediums including sculpting and watercolor.

cards.headline: Florida students reach milestone with 60% testing at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking exam.
cards.body:
For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, making this year's results a meaningful climb in student performance across the state.

The improvement extended to Florida's schools overall. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B grade, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning As jumped from 44% to 51%.

hero.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
hero.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following Facebook comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made errors in her recommendation, stating that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, in which he labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, constituted a "serious offense" that justified his removal.

According to an investigation report, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that determined disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald be reinstated and awarded back pay and benefits. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald will be rehired. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises broader questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. No timeline for a final decision has been announced.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as inflation drives up food prices
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check, including comparing stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, cutting down food waste, and beginning with a meal plan.

hero.headline: Anthem Blue Cross denies breast cancer patient's reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
hero.teaser: A breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled in Treasure Coast.
hero.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and argues that insurance companies should reconsider their coverage policies. She says the product produces fewer complications than other options with proven success. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem responded by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and that without FDA approval, the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council moves forward with Midway Road Turnpike interchange, $95 million widening project
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance in June to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange will improve accessibility to accommodate growth that has already occurred and will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike. The partial interchange is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. The community has launched a fundraiser to help her fiance rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a fire at her Hobe Sound home on Monday. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. White's fiancé Mark learned of her death and has since received community support through a fundraiser launched by friends to help him rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who knew White for eight years, described her as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves people," Fenn said. The loss carries additional weight for Mark, who previously lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death is further compounded by timing, as her birthday was the Fourth of July and she died just days before. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to wrap by next Fourth of July. The upgrade will nearly double the facility's capacity, expanding available slips from 18 to 44 for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will add a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the improvements serve dual purposes: expanding capacity and strengthening the dock against severe weather. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

The city is working to accommodate businesses during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger tours from the dock, was initially uncertain about continuing operations. The city found a solution by allowing the business to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section for passenger boarding. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, described the compromise as workable. He noted the dock's current limitations, particularly on weekends when demand peaks. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," Kuyrkendall said, emphasizing the dock's importance to the city's identity and economy.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams pulled out of her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday after injuring her right knee during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
The 44-year-old Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. In an Instagram post, Serena said she did everything she could but her knee was not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that wasn't scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again soon, telling followers to "stay tuned to a city near you." Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Defending champion Argentina edges Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance in World Cup
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina survived a scare from underdog Cape Verde in a World Cup Round of 32 match that went to extra time in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina defeated Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a thrilling World Cup match that required extra time to decide. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Lionel Messi scored in the 29th minute for a 1-0 lead, taking a quick touch on a lofted pass from Martinez and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha. The goal was Messi's record-extending 20th career World Cup goal and his seventh of this tournament. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, made 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is targeting a state title in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite the successful regular season, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to pursue greater postseason success. Head coach Jimmy Robertson is building the team around a veteran senior class, with most seniors having played together since middle school. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To elevate their performance, the Scots have scheduled more demanding opponents for the 2026 season. Senior Jack Williams said the tougher schedule is designed to help the team compete at a higher level and attract new talent. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete," Williams said. For the Scots, success this season is measured by postseason advancement rather than regular season record alone. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that going farther than the second round of playoffs is the primary goal, adding "that's all that matters."

Between June 20 and June 26 alone, Donalds raised nearly $2 million, with major contributors including GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. Donalds has invested heavily in his campaign with a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms. He has also consolidated endorsements from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison.

In stark contrast, Lt. Gov. Jay Collins raised only $15,500 in hard money and $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the same week, with less than $3.5 million total as of June 26. Collins struggled during a Friday night debate, fumbling answers on issues ranging from data centers to voting for DeSantis in 2018, which he could not do because he was not a Florida resident at that time. Collins lost his temper at various points during the debate and needed notes to help with responses.

cards.headline: Florida students reach milestone with 60% testing at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking exam.
cards.body:
For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, making this year's results a meaningful climb in student performance across the state.

The improvement extended to Florida's schools overall. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B grade, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning As jumped from 44% to 51%.

cards.headline: Four Florida municipalities receive $7.2 million in FEMA grants for Hurricane Ian recovery
cards.teaser: FloridaCommerce announced $7.2 million in FEMA grants for Charlotte County, Port of the Islands, Seminole County, and Palatka to fund infrastructure projects related to Hurricane Ian recovery and future storm preparedness.
cards.body:
FloridaCommerce announced it is distributing $7.2 million in grants through the Hurricane Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program. The FEMA funds are designed to provide infrastructure recovery and improve emergency preparedness following the Category 4 storm that hit Florida in September 2022. Local governments must match the same amount of local money to complete the projects.

Charlotte County will receive $5.83 million for a public works hurricane-safe room generator and $93,392 for a leachate waste plant generator project. The Port of the Islands Community Improvement District has $750,840 earmarked for a Union Road water storage and infrastructure retrofit project. Seminole County has $319,437 for a mitigation reconstruction project on Shad Lane, and the city of Palatka has $283,996 for a lift station generator. Secretary of Commerce J. Alex Kelly said the funding supports Governor Ron DeSantis' commitment to strengthening the state's long-term resiliency. The Ian HMGMP program has already distributed more than $12 million in grants to municipalities following Hurricane Ian, which made landfall near Fort Myers on September 22, 2022.

cards.headline: President Trump's actions draw comparisons to monarchy as nation marks 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: The 250th anniversary of America's independence from Britain has sparked debate about presidential power, as President Donald Trump's second term actions lead historians to draw parallels with King George III.
cards.body:
The 250th anniversary of America's liberation from a king opened with a campaign-style rally on the National Mall by President Donald Trump, whose face adorns banners fluttering from federal buildings across the nation's capital. Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered the Department of Justice to pursue his political enemies, deployed the U.S. Marines to the nation's second largest city, and leveraged the presidency to enrich himself and his family. He has demanded that comedians who mock him be fired, slapped his name on the Kennedy Center, pushed to seize control of elections, filed lawsuits against news organizations whose coverage he disliked, and sued his own government seeking $10 billion in taxpayer money.

Trump's actions have drawn comparisons to King George III, the British monarch whose rule inspired the American Revolution. Trump rejected the comparison in a CBS "60 Minutes" interview, saying "I'm not a king. If I was a king, I wouldn't be dealing with you." Princeton University historian Julian Zelizer said the label reflects how Trump perceives himself and the presidency. When King Charles III visited Trump, the official White House X account posted an image of both men captioned "TWO KINGS." At the start of his second term, Trump posted "LONG LIVE THE KING" after announcing he had ended a New York City transportation program.

cards.headline: Americans express measured views on nation's 250th birthday amid political divisions
cards.teaser: As the United States celebrates its 250th birthday, many Americans are focusing on local community and personal concepts of patriotism rather than national political divisions.
cards.body:
Across the United States, many Americans are celebrating their country's 250th birthday by tuning into their own personal concepts of America rather than focusing on partisan divisions. In Associated Press interviews with citizens in the days before the Fourth, auto technician Joe Fuqua-Bejarano in Topeka, Kansas, said resilience, not politics, makes Americans awesome as a people. "We've just all got to find unity somewhere, whether that's in laughter or perseverance, and keep everybody cool," he said from the fireworks stand where he works a side hustle.

Christina Zhou, a 25-year-old research assistant from Cambridge, Massachusetts, acknowledged there are lots of points of contention but also beautiful things happening. "What I'm trying to do is think about just things that are happening locally," she said. "It feels a little bit more like within our own personal control." In Mont Vernon, New Hampshire, farmer Mindy Dean, 50, said the 250th celebrations have been mostly lost on her. "We're just happy Americans. We kinda do our own thing and just enjoy our freedom as Americans," she said. Neil Casey, an 81-year-old retiree from Nashua, New Hampshire, and his friend Maureen Regan are visiting Boston's historical sites and Fourth of July events, with Regan noting that World Cup soccer fans who visited praised the country.

cards.headline: European World Cup fans face economic pressures at home despite extended U.S. visits
cards.teaser: While European soccer fans appear to have escaped work for extended World Cup trips to the United States, rising tax burdens and aging populations are straining the welfare systems that fund their vacation time.
cards.body:
Europeans traveling through the United States for the World Cup do have more vacation time than most Americans. Under European Union rules, workers are entitled to at least four weeks of paid annual leave, with many countries and collective agreements offering additional time. However, the OECD's 2025 tax-wedge numbers reveal the cost of this bargain. Belgium was highest at 52.5% for a single average worker, followed by Germany at 49.3%, France at 47.2%, Austria at 47.1%, and Italy at 45.8%, compared to the OECD average of 35.1%. The tax wedge measures the gap between what it costs to employ a worker and what that worker takes home after income tax and social-security contributions.

Europe built much of its welfare state for societies with more children, stronger growth and more young contributors. On January 1, 2025, 22% of the EU population was already 65 or older. Eurostat projects the working-age share of the EU population, those aged 20 to 64, to fall from 58% in 2025 to 50% by 2100. Germany's public pension depends heavily on today's workers paying for today's retirees, with the regular retirement age already rising to 67 for Germans born in 1964 or later. A government-appointed pension commission has discussed a Swedish-style funded pension element, mandatory contributions, and a gradual increase in the retirement age linked to life expectancy, a path that could eventually push retirement toward 70.

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man died early Sunday morning following a serious collision on State Road 710 in Martin County, Florida Highway Patrol officials reported. The crash took place around 2 a.m. at the intersection near Southwest Silver Fox Lane on the roadway also known as Beeline Highway.

According to the Florida Highway Patrol, a northbound 2015 Kia Optima crossed over into the southbound lane and struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on. The impact occurred on the left front sections of both vehicles. The force of the collision caused the Kia to catch fire immediately. The vehicle came to rest on the grass shoulder, still facing north. The Tundra, meanwhile, ended up facing southeast in the southbound lane after the crash.

The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, identified as a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, suffered injuries in the crash and was airlifted by Lifestar helicopter to a hospital for treatment.

The Florida Highway Patrol is conducting an ongoing investigation into the circumstances that led to the crash. State Road 710 serves as a major transportation corridor connecting communities throughout western Martin County.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves Crain Estate, hosts artists from around the world in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as a vibrant artistic destination while maintaining the historic Crain Estate. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who formerly lived on the property. Jaxson Crain worked as a tile worker, and evidence of his skilled craftsmanship appears throughout the facility in the flooring, walls, and ceilings. According to art director Krystal Masters, the estate remains 90% unchanged from the Crains' era. Guided tours of the lush gardens and distinctive architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Visitors can explore the smoking and bourbon room, which features oak paneling, masculine colors, and pre-stained glass that opens to a patio bar. The couple traveled globally nine times, acquiring unique items for their Florida home, including a gazebo shipped from India that features decorative peacocks.

The estate takes its name from the peacocks that have inhabited the grounds for decades. The Crains introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, and the population has since grown to over 100 birds. Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp, has become a beloved resident. He lives in a dedicated space, has his own bowls, and receives daily hand-feeding from staff. Tour guides note that visitors, particularly children, treasure the experience of feeding the peacocks directly. The foundation has made deliberate choices to preserve the estate's original character and resist commercialization.

The artist-in-residency program draws creative professionals from around the world, providing simple yet elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab welcomes both children and adults of all experience levels, with Krystal offering one-on-one instruction for complete beginners. Students explore various mediums including sculpting and watercolor painting. Current workshops include "Paint Your Pet in Watercolor and Rainbow." According to Krystal, the majority of her classes are individual sessions where people "come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art."

For Krystal, art serves a therapeutic purpose beyond creative expression. "Art is a form of therapy and it destresses people," she explains. Her goal is helping students leave feeling fulfilled and disconnected from daily distractions. Seeing participants walk away satisfied drives her commitment to the foundation's mission. Through its combination of historical preservation, artist support, and accessible art education, the Peacock House Art Foundation continues transforming Fort Pierce into a meaningful cultural hub.
